questions.question: What does 'href' stand for in <a href="...">?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: href stands for Hypertext Reference. It's the attribute that specifies the destination URL of the link.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: href stands for Hypertext Reference. It's the attribute that specifies the destination URL of the link.

questions.question: Which attribute makes a link open in a new tab?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: target="_blank" makes a link open in a new tab or window. This keeps your website open while users explore the linked content.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: What does #contact in a link do?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: #contact creates an anchor link that jumps to an element with id="contact" on the same page. The # indicates an ID selector.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

correct.details: Links without href are placeholder links - they look like links but don't go anywhere. Useful during development before you have the actual URLs.

questions.question: What color are unvisited links typically?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Unvisited links are typically blue by default in most browsers. Visited links are usually purple, and active links (being clicked) are red.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: Why avoid 'click here' link text?
options: It's not descriptive for screen readers
questions.correct_answer: It's not descriptive for screen readers

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: "Click here" is not descriptive for screen reader users who often navigate by links. Instead, use descriptive text like "Download the PDF guide".
